topology_reasoning.device_identification: The bitmap is a single-input, four-output multimode splitter or star-coupler style device. A narrow left access waveguide expands through a short taper into a wide rectangular multimode body. Four right-side access waveguides are placed at distinct vertical offsets and connect back to the body through taper transitions before continuing as straight ports.
topology_reasoning.operation: The wide central block supports multimode interference or slab propagation from the input taper. The four output tapers sample the field at selected vertical positions and convert the local wide-body field into single-mode output guides. The function is defined primarily by the multimode-body length and width, the input/output taper widths and lengths, the output guide width, and the output vertical offsets/gaps.
topology_reasoning.implementation_plan: Use only primitive rectangles, tapers, and straights on layer (1,0). Overlap the tapers with the multimode body edge and rely on GDS polygon overlap/rasterization rather than raw polygon stitching. Keep all geometry controlled by top-level tunables. Emit lengths.json with body_length as the length-like delta knob so verify_knob_response can prove a real geometry response.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only model: one body rectangle, one left taper, four right tapers, and four output rectangles. Widths snapped to the gdsfactory 2 nm port grid; write_gds uses with_metadata=False so verifier can see the real top cell.
